gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, of Chigee's two 5-inch units, only the AIO-5 Play can run from a USB cable and move between bikes. Chigee says that with a $9 USB adapter cable and spare ACC cables 'to use the same device across different bikes'. The AIO-5 Lite is listed as 'Hardwired (Battery + ACC wire)' only.
standout_why: I compared this against throttlebuff.com, which says only that the AIO-5 Lite 'needs a power connection' and covers the Play only in its BMW edition. I also compared it against motorcyclegpshub.com, which has no AIO-5 Play or Lite entry and gives power details only for the Carpuride W502 Pro and W702 Pro (12V harness plus a 5V/2.5A USB cable) and the BMW-cradle W702BS Pro. ChatGPT's own chigee.com results include the comparison page that holds this row, but its answer never used it. I could not open the three Handlebar HQ pages (self-signed certificate error), so I could not check them. Neither rival I read names the Carpuride exclusions (Huawei P and Mate series, all HarmonyOS phones), and motorcyclegpshub gives only 'Android 11 or newer with 5 GHz Wi-Fi'.
decides: For a shopper who asked for 'portable', this confirms the AIO-5 Play ($399.99) as the Chigee to pick and rules out the AIO-5 Lite from ChatGPT's search. The Lite cannot take USB power and needs a battery-plus-ACC hardwire on each bike. For the Carpuride W702/W502 ($269.99 today, not the $279.99 ChatGPT showed), Huawei P or Mate and HarmonyOS phone owners should be steered away. Android Auto needs Android 8.0 or newer, and Carpuride recommends Android 11 or newer. Battery-only portability still points to the Aoocci F5 ($189 on aoocci.com today against ChatGPT's $199), but I could not source its battery or compatibility specs.
